labelChirho: to lust after, be infatuated with
descriptionChirho: The verb in Qal perfect and consecutive imperfect (3fs) meaning 'to lust after, to be sexually infatuated with,' used of Jerusalem/Samaria personified as a woman lusting after foreign nations (Ezek 23:5, 7, 9, 12, 16, 20). The finite verbal forms consistently express the action of passionate, illicit desire. Multilingual evidence: eng 'she lusted / and she lusted', spa 'se apasionó / y se apasionó', arb 'عَشِقَتْ / فَعَشِقَتْ', kor '열망했다', swa 'alitamani / na akawatamani', hin 'ललचाई वह'.

The Qal active participle (masculine plural) used substantivally to denote 'lovers, paramours' -- those who are the objects or agents of illicit passion, distinct from the verbal action of lusting itself. Found in Ezek 23:5 referring to the Assyrians as Samaria's 'lovers.' The substantivized participle functions as a noun designating persons, not an action. Multilingual evidence: eng 'lovers', spa 'los amantes', arb 'عُشَّاقٌ' (broken plural, nominal form), kor '연인들이', swa 'wapenzi wako', hin 'प्रेमियों ने'.
